threads.body: [General] Reuse the stable `ServiceAttributes.SERVICE_NAME` and `SERVICE_VERSION` constants instead of redefining their keys. Their names and types match, and `.github/instructions/instrumentation-library.instructions.md:13–15` requires importing matching stable constants. `ManifestResourceProvider` already follows this pattern. This is non-blocking.

Is it worth setting schema URL to `https://opentelemetry.io/schemas/1.40.0` to match the SDK's service detector? With declarative detectors ordered `manifest` then `service`, that would let their descriptions merge when the service names match, rather than dropping the manifest's `service.version` because the schema URLs differ.

Though that's pretty fragile and not sure how we'd keep these in sync?

replies.body: What if opentelemetry-java was updated to always pin to the latest semconv schema url? If both opentelemetry-java and opentelemetry-java-instrumentation use a convention to always use the latest, then they always agree yeah? Although, while I think it will be straight forward for opentelemetry-java to stay at the latest, maybe there are reasons opentelemetry-java-instrumenation would want to delay? If so, that would create a conflict.

we emit different schema urls (versions) in different places, but in this particular place, we can pin to opentelemetry-java's version. i'm not sure I trust "latest" in case there's a semconv release in between the sdk and instrumentation releases, maybe can add a test here that loads the entity both ways and fail if we get the bad merge behavior?

> maybe can add a test here that loads the entity both ways and fail if we get the bad merge behavior?

Good idea. Implemented in 76b6ee9b5d:

- New test utility class for extracting the entity schema url from core and asserting that a given resource's schema url and entity schema urls match it
- Updated ServiceResource to set the same schema url version as core
- Update all tests to leverage the new assertion utility
